best_for: People on Mac or Linux, or on mixed machines, who want a KeePass-compatible password manager with browser autofill built in and no subscription or cloud account.

points.title: No cloud, no subscription
points.text: KeePassXC keeps passwords in an encrypted file on your disk and sends nothing to remote servers. It is free and open source, with no ads or subscriptions.

points.title: Opens KeePass files
points.text: It uses the KDBX 3.1 and KDBX 4 formats, so the same database works in KeePass on Windows. Old KeePass 1.x files can be imported but not saved back.

points.title: Built-in extras, no plugins
points.text: Browser autofill through the KeePassXC-Browser extension, TOTP codes, passkeys and an SSH agent link are built in. KeePass2 plugins do not work, and the team has no plans to support them.

points.title: Sync is up to you
points.text: There is no built-in sync. Put the database in a cloud folder you already use, and keep any key file off that cloud, for example on a USB stick.

points.title: A YubiKey is not true 2FA here
points.text: YubiKey and OnlyKey challenge-response strengthen the database key, but the FAQ says it is not a real second factor. Keep a copy of the key's secret, or losing the key can lock you out.

points.title: Windows 7 and old Macs stay behind
points.text: Current builds need Windows 10 or 11 (with the MSVC redistributable) or macOS 12. Windows 7 to 8.1 can use the legacy 2.7.12 installer. The MSI installs for all users, on x64 and Arm64, and the Windows listing keeps 21 versions.

points.title: Flatpak is the Linux pick
points.text: The project recommends its Flathub build, published by the KeePassXC Team and marked verified, for x64 and Arm64. macOS and Linux list only the current release here.
